ChurchStream is free software for **Seventh-day Adventist churches**: live streaming to YouTube and Facebook plus projection of hymns, Bible readings and announcements, from one simple control panel. It runs on Windows and Mac.

## Download

| Computer | Download |
|---|---|
| **Windows** laptop or PC | **[ChurchStream-win-x64.zip](https://github.com/driviere/churchStream/releases/download/v0.5.0/ChurchStream-win-x64.zip)** |
| **Mac with an Apple chip** (M1–M4) | **[ChurchStream-mac-arm64.zip](https://github.com/driviere/churchStream/releases/download/v0.5.0/ChurchStream-mac-arm64.zip)** |
| **Mac with an Intel processor** | **[ChurchStream-mac-x64.zip](https://github.com/driviere/churchStream/releases/download/v0.5.0/ChurchStream-mac-x64.zip)** |

**Updating?** Copy the new files over your old ChurchStream folder; your **ChurchStream-data** folder (settings, songs, services) is kept. First time? See the install steps in the [README](https://github.com/driviere/churchStream#install-windows).

## New in 0.5.0

The stream page becomes a small studio: scenes, a Preview before things go on air, smooth transitions, up to four cameras, a sound mixer, titles and keyboard shortcuts. The main control panel stays as simple as before.

### Scenes, Preview and Program, transitions
- Open the **stream page** (**/stream**, address in **Settings → Phones & tablets**). **Preview** (left) shows what goes on air next; **Program** (right) is what viewers see.
- **Quick** mode: click a scene and it goes on air. **Studio** mode: a click puts it in Preview; press **Cut**, **Auto** or pull the **T-bar**.
- Transitions: **Cut, Fade, Dip to black, Slide and Wipe**, 0.3 to 2 seconds. They happen inside the stream, so they look smooth for viewers and in the recording.
- **Scenes** combine up to four pictures: two cameras side by side, the slides with the preacher in a corner, four cameras at once. **+ New scene** opens an editor where you drag and resize pictures, choose a layout, add a border or crop. Group scenes into tabs such as "Sermon" or "Music".
- **Sources** shows every camera, the slides and videos live, side by side.
- Names, the ticker and a playing video stay on top through every scene change.

### Up to four cameras
- Add **cameras 3 and 4** in **Settings → Camera & sound** (USB, network or phone cameras) and give each a name, such as "Pulpit". If one stops, the stream carries on and it comes back by itself.

### Sound mixer
- A fader, mute and level bar for each sound: the microphone or sound desk, videos and music, a second microphone, and the whole stream. Changes are instant and remembered.

### Titles and pictures
- **Titles:** Scripture, Sermon title, Speaker or Welcome, in three styles (Classic, Modern bar, Minimal). **Use the reading on screen** fills in the Bible reading.
- **Pictures:** your logo, a QR code for giving or a flyer, in a corner, lower middle or full screen.

### Keyboard shortcuts (and Stream Deck)
- **1–9** scenes, **Space** Cut, **Enter** Auto, **D** dip to black, **F1–F4** cameras, **G** picture, **N** name, **T** ticker, **R** recording. Press **?** for the list. A Stream Deck can press them with its *Hotkey* action.

### Less computer power
- The pictures for the stream page are only made while someone is watching them, empty names and captions aren't drawn, and the video and music feed rests between videos. On our test computer the stream with the studio uses about a tenth of a processor core more than streaming alone; without the studio, about the same as before.
- Videos played into the stream now keep their sound and picture together within about 30 ms.
- On a computer that struggles, **Settings → Advanced → Studio** switches back to the simple switching.

### Control panel
- While a stream page is open, the control panel hides its camera and "Stream shows" switches and says the stream is run from the stream page. When it closes, the control panel takes over again.

**Mac:** ChurchStream now brings its own FFmpeg for Macs (Apple chip and Intel), so the studio works on Macs too. Replace ChurchStream.app in Applications with the new one. **Windows:** copy the new files over your ChurchStream folder. Your settings and songs in ChurchStream-data are kept.

**Please try the studio at church** before relying on it on Sabbath, with your own cameras and computer.

## Good to know
- Projecting or streaming hymns still under copyright needs your church's **CCLI** licence (and the Streaming Licence for online use).
- ChurchStream is an independent project, not an official product of the Seventh-day Adventist Church.
